title: Chapter 6: Union Executive – President, Vice President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

blocks.content: There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.

rows: Elected members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi and Puducherry)
All members (both elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament only
Must be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
Must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha
Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces
Ex-Officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Impeachment under Article 61 requiring special 2/3rd majority of total membership in both Houses
Resolution passed by effective majority in Rajya Sabha and agreed to by Lok Sabha

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The President is the head of the Indian State, the first citizen of India, and acts as the symbol of unity, integrity, and solidarity of the nation.
The Prime Minister is the real executive authority (de facto executive), whereas the President is the nominal executive authority (de jure executive).
The Vice-President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and officiates as President during temporary vacancies.
Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 restricted the total number of ministers, including the PM, to 15 percent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

Impeachment of the President (Article 61) can be initiated in either House of Parliament for 'violation of the Constitution' and requires a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House.
Nominated members of Parliament do not participate in the Presidential election, but they do participate in the impeachment of the President and the election of the Vice-President.
The power of the President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament is governed under Article 123.
